title: Step 19 diagonal toric fixed-corner lowest-jet matching
smooth_diagonal_ansatz_scope: For adjacent labels ±e1, ±e2, a diagonal fiber matrix with p vanishing on e1-rods and q on e2-rods satisfies the local smoothness parity conditions of Lemma 2.2: p^2=r^2+r^4 even, q^2=t^2 mu(r,0)^2+t^4 even, b=0 in r^2 t^2 R_even. This confirms local smoothness of the diagonal ansatz at standard-basis corners; it does not cover arbitrary labels.
interpretation: The corner zeroth-order equations are consistent for arbitrary u/A once a and b are chosen as exact functions of u. With A=-K_B(0)=2u, both a and b equal -(2A+1)/6, exactly the Step-15 rod ODE cubic coefficient for a constant-curvature rod. Thus the standard-basis diagonal corner imposes no lowest-jet cap on A: adjacent large-negative-curvature rods can meet smoothly to this order. Any obstruction must enter through higher jets, finite-length matching/holonomy, nonlocal polygon compatibility, the spectral/eigenfunction condition, or through the full matrix/twist system.
caution: This is a lowest-jet exact-Einstein corner calculation, not a pinched global construction and not a proof that all large-A rods close.
